hero.title: Seventy years in. **Time for a reset.**
hero.lede: Roseville more than tripled in size during the 1950s, so many yards here have had about 70 years to settle, fill in and wear out. HD Landscape clears what is tired and sets the yard up for the way you use it now.
chips: Water sent away from the house

about.title: A 1950s town on **heavy, slow ground.**
body: Roseville grew from 15,816 people in 1950 to 50,195 in 1960. A third of its homes date to the 1950s and another fifth to the 1960s, and the joint parks plan for Roseville and Eastpointe calls both cities entirely built out. So the work here is rarely a blank slate. It is an existing yard that has been filling in and settling for decades.
The land is level. USDA soil maps put nearly the whole city at slopes of 2 percent or less, so a yard here gets no help from the lay of the land when it rains.

The soil is the part you cannot see. The same maps rate nearly all of the city somewhat poorly drained or worse, mostly Sims clay loam, Lenawee silty clay loam and Blount loam. On level ground with heavy soil, rain stays where it lands unless somebody gives it a way out.

points.title: Water comes first
points.body: A low spot by the foundation or a soggy side yard will undo a new bed, so [yard grading](/yard-grading/) belongs ahead of any planting or [sod](/sod-installation/).

points.title: Beds past their prime
points.body: Shrubs planted decades ago are often up past the windows and bare at the bottom. We pull what has had its run, roots and all, and [replant](/plant-installation/) with fewer plants that fit the space.

points.title: Shade is scarce here
points.body: Macomb County says the area along and below the Clinton River is among the most lacking in tree canopy in southeast Michigan, after Dutch elm disease and emerald ash borer. So a healthy tree here should get [a good trim](/tree-trimming-and-removal/) long before it comes down.

points.title: A yard can slide between tenants
points.body: About one home in three here is rented. We do one time [cleanups](/spring-and-fall-cleanups/), [hedge trimming](/hedge-trimming/) and [mulching](/mulching/) for owners and landlords, and for new buyers catching up on a yard, with the work spelled out line by line first.

logistics.title: Roseville is close to home for us.
body: We are based in St. Clair Shores, the next town east, so Jake does not have far to come for a look at the yard. You hear what he would do first and what can wait, then comes an itemized estimate to go over line by line.

Where a side yard is tight, we plan where material sits and how the old beds and sod come out before the truck arrives. The estimate covers how the debris gets out, and the walks get left clean. A tree between the walk and the street is a question for the city, so ask there before it gets cut, even if we are the ones holding the saw.

facts.label: Ground
facts.value: Level clay and loam, slow to drain

faq.q: Do you landscape in Roseville, MI?
faq.a: Yes. HD Landscape works in Roseville, and it is close to home, since we are based next door in St. Clair Shores. Older yards here tend to need a reset, which can mean [landscape renovation](/landscape-renovation/), [yard grading](/yard-grading/), [sod](/sod-installation/), [hedge trimming](/hedge-trimming/), [mulching](/mulching/) or [cleanups](/spring-and-fall-cleanups/). We also do [pressure washing](/pressure-washing-roseville-mi/). No sprinklers and no lawn aeration.

faq.q: What should I fix first in an older yard?
faq.a: Start with the water, then what is in the ground, then what goes on top. On Roseville's level, slow ground, that means getting the grade right so rain moves away from the house. Take out what is overgrown or dying. Then plant, lay sod and finish with [mulch](/mulching/). Doing it in that order means you only pay for the work once, and if you want to spread it over two seasons, ask Jake where the sensible stopping point is.

faq.q: Why does my yard stay soggy?
faq.a: Most of Roseville sits on clay and loam soils that drain slowly, on very level ground. A low spot, a settled foundation bed or a downspout with nowhere to go can keep a yard wet for days. [Yard grading](/yard-grading/) helps with surface water. It will not help a sewer backup in a big storm, which is a question for a plumber and the city.

faq.q: Can you clean up a rental or a house I just bought?
faq.a: Yes. In Roseville that is a good use of a one-time visit. We clear beds, cut back shrubs, pull weeds, trim hedges and leave the place looking cared for. Text Jake a few photos of the yard and he can say what he would tackle first. If you want it kept up after that, ask about [monthly maintenance](/monthly-landscape-maintenance/).

faq.q: Do you trim trees in Roseville?
faq.a: Yes. We prune trees and take down smaller ones on your property. A big removal is tree company work, and the first walk settles which kind of job you have. See [tree trimming and removal](/tree-trimming-and-removal/) for more. For a tree between the walk and the street, ask the city first.
